purpose: Independent practice of B1.6 (fair-share with up to 10 sharers, 20 items).
student_learning_goal: I can share up to 20 items fairly between 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, or 10 friends and write the result with a mixed number when needed.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can share up to 20 items fairly between 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, or 10 friends and write the result with a mixed number when needed.
header.character_watermark: Sammy the Sharer in the top-right corner with paper plates. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Share fairly with no leftovers. Draw what each plate gets. Write the per-plate count.
parts.visual_layout: Top of the page. Four sharing scenes in a 2x2 grid.

image_placeholders.description: Four sharing scenes in B&W line-art, 2-row × 2-column grid. Each scene ~3.5in × 1.8in. Scene A: 12 treats, 4 plates. Scene B: 15 treats, 5 plates. Scene C: 20 treats, 4 plates. Scene D: 16 treats, 8 plates.
image_placeholders.placement: Top of the page; four scenes in 2x2 grid.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P1_FOUR_EVEN: keywords (plates) name what the scenes show.

parts.student_instructions: Find the leftover and cut it as a fraction. Write your answer as a mixed number.
parts.visual_layout: Middle. Four sharing scenes in a 2x2 grid with pre-drawn fraction-lines.

image_placeholders.description: Four sharing scenes in B&W line-art, 2-row × 2-column grid. Each ~3.5in × 1.8in. Scene A: 18 treats, 8 plates (one leftover-set with pre-drawn fourth-lines). Scene B: 14 treats, 4 plates (one leftover-set with pre-drawn half-line). Scene C: 17 treats, 5 plates (leftover with pre-drawn fifths). Scene D: 16 treats, 6 plates (leftover with pre-drawn thirds).
image_placeholders.placement: Middle of the page; four scenes in 2x2 grid.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P2_FOUR_MIXED: keywords (fraction) name what the scenes show.

parts.student_instructions: Sammy has 20 treats. List 5 different ways he could share them fairly between 2-10 friends. Write each as a division equation.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. A blank box with thinking-bubble icon.

image_placeholders.description: A blank rectangular drawing box in B&W line-art, ~7in × 2.5in, with light-grey solid outline. Sammy thinking-bubble icon in the top-right corner.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P3_CHOICE_BOX: keywords (share, ways) name what the box asks for.

parts.answer_key: Even shares only: 20÷2=10, 20÷4=5, 20÷5=4, 20÷10=2. Plus 20÷1=20 and 20÷20=1. Children may also list: 20÷3 = 6 2/3, 20÷6 = 3 1/3, 20÷8 = 2 1/2 (mixed-number shares — also valid).

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, write your own sharing scenario with 19 items and 4 friends. Solve.
teacher_notes: Lesson 4 consolidation. Watch for: (a) Part 2 children who can deal but can't match the fraction — flag for matching-rule reteach; (b) Part 2 D (16÷6) — the trickiest, requiring 4 leftovers cut into thirds; (c) Part 3 children who only list even-divisor answers — coaching opportunity for mixed-number alternatives.
